parts:
Good morning Chris,

I am currently trying to make my way through your guide in order to see how the package runs etc with some test data of my own. however, I seem to have hit a stumbling block when it comes to setting the graph level attributes. This then displays a message to "check the following vertex names:' and proceeds to list a number (around 60 of all of the DK atlas regions; the error list is below).

I realized that I had failed to include the "N <- which(abs(densities - 0.10) < 0.001)" line when initializing my variables. messages.author: dadcb4fd6a01f8d1
messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] issue with assign_lobes(g)
parts:
Hi Daniel,
Regarding the error in "assign_lobes", it is probably because "_thickness" is at the end of region names. You can remove these using "sed" (on Linux):
sed -i 's/_thickness//g' FILE

Regarding the variable "N", if you are referring to the line of code that says "corrs[[1]][[N]]$threshold", I simply included that to illustrate how to access the correlation threshold for each density (in this case, for the graph with 10% density). This was for space-saving reasons in the Guide, and I use it other times if I am focusing on a specific graph density to save code. It is not required and you can safely skip it.

Let me know if these fix your issues.
Chris

messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] issue with assign_lobes(g)
parts:
Could you send the complete command line that you used for that? It may not be completely clear in the User Guide, but the full command spans 3 lines.

g <- Map(function(x, y) llply(x, ...

In this case, "function(x, y)" is an *anonymous function*. The "x" is a "placeholder" for a certain variable, here it is "g" (on the 3rd line in the code block), and "y" is a placeholder for "as.list(groups)". The "Map" function takes those two variables and "steps" through their elements. So it is similar to a "for" loop in that sense. If you have 3 groups, then the "g" variable should be a list object with 3 elements, and "as.list(groups)" should also have 3 elements (assuming you created a variable for your group names).

Try that and let me know if it works.
Chris

messages.subject: Re: [brainGraph-help] issue with assign_lobes(g)
parts:
Yes, those are all empty graphs, so the problem would occur before "Map", and in fact before the initial graph creation step (Chapter 4.5.2 of the User Guide).

The fact that your residuals are all 1's does suggest a problem specifically with the "get.resid" function. This is one of the earlier functions I wrote so it is not as polished as it could be. The first thing to check would be the "all.dat.tidy" object, which is a *data.table* that is the covariates table merged with the LH + RH thickness data. If you wouldn't mind, you can either post the first several lines of this object in an email, or send me the data themselves.
One problem with "get.resid" is that it isn't very smart when it comes to creating a formula for regressing out the effects of covariates on thickness. It will basically take every column in your "covars" table (excluding Study.ID). If you do not have a "Study.ID" column, then there will be a problem. If you have covariates of no interest or covariates that, when included, alter the interpretability of a linear model, there will be problems. So please check to see that "covars" contains exactly the columns you are interested in regressing out (for one of my studies that was "Age", "Sex", and "Site").

Chris

Sorry I just noticed that you said there was a warning. Could you please additionally post the exact warning?

And a bit more RE the last few lines of code you included:

The function call to "get.resid" assigns that function's output object to "all.dat.resids". The subsequent lines are simply assigning new objects to the elements of the list "all.dat.resids". The dollar sign operator just allows you to call the element by name. Since you're coming from Matlab, this is more-or-less equivalent to a *struct*, where the equivalent line might be
all_dat_tidy = all_dat_resids.all_dat_tidy

(names changed because I don't remember if Matlab allows a "dot" in a variable name)
If you've used SPM, then this would be similar to getting elements of the SPM struct by e.g. "SPM.xX", "SPM.Sess.U", etc.

On Tue, Jan 24, 2017 at 12:45 PM, Chris Watson <cwa...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
Yes, those are all empty graphs, so the problem would occur before "Map", and in fact before the initial graph creation step (Chapter 4.5.2 of the User Guide).

The fact that your residuals are all 1's does suggest a problem specifically with the "get.resid" function. This is one of the earlier functions I wrote so it is not as polished as it could be. The first thing to check would be the "all.dat.tidy" object, which is a *data.table* that is the covariates table merged with the LH + RH thickness data. If you wouldn't mind, you can either post the first several lines of this object in an email, or send me the data themselves.
One problem with "get.resid" is that it isn't very smart when it comes to creating a formula for regressing out the effects of covariates on thickness. It will basically take every column in your "covars" table (excluding Study.ID). If you do not have a "Study.ID" column, then there will be a problem. If you have covariates of no interest or covariates that, when included, alter the interpretability of a linear model, there will be problems. So please check to see that "covars" contains exactly the columns you are interested in regressing out (for one of my studies that was "Age", "Sex", and "Site").

Chris

On Monday, January 23, 2017 at 5:23:41 PM UTC, Chris Watson wrote:
Could you send the complete command line that you used for that? It may not be completely clear in the User Guide, but the full command spans 3 lines.

g <- Map(function(x, y) llply(x, ...

In this case, "function(x, y)" is an *anonymous function*. The "x" is a "placeholder" for a certain variable, here it is "g" (on the 3rd line in the code block), and "y" is a placeholder for "as.list(groups)". The "Map" function takes those two variables and "steps" through their elements. So it is similar to a "for" loop in that sense. If you have 3 groups, then the "g" variable should be a list object with 3 elements, and "as.list(groups)" should also have 3 elements (assuming you created a variable for your group names).

Try that and let me know if it works.
Chris

On Monday, January 23, 2017 at 1:38:19 PM UTC, Chris Watson wrote:
Hi Daniel,
Regarding the error in "assign_lobes", it is probably because "_thickness" is at the end of region names. You can remove these using "sed" (on Linux):
sed -i 's/_thickness//g' FILE

Regarding the variable "N", if you are referring to the line of code that says "corrs[[1]][[N]]$threshold", I simply included that to illustrate how to access the correlation threshold for each density (in this case, for the graph with 10% density). This was for space-saving reasons in the Guide, and I use it other times if I am focusing on a specific graph density to save code. It is not required and you can safely skip it.

Let me know if these fix your issues.
Chris

parts:
Thanks, I saw the output in the other email. It looks correct to me. (BTW, you don't have to type "list()", as that "creates" a list object; for a data.table you just type the variable name and it prints the first and last 5 lines)

The warning you posted suggests that you have a repeat row in the data. The reason you see all 1's in the result is because it would equal the length of each "observation" (or combination of variables). This would also suggest that "resids.all" should have at least one value that is *not* equal to 1 (perhaps 2, or more if there are more repeats). The probable culprit in the event of a repeat would be "Study.ID", so please check to see that there isn't a duplicate ID somewhere.

Chris
